name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default but auto-switch to light mode when the system detects high ambient light. This keeps eye strain low in dim rooms while ensuring readability in bright spaces—no manual toggling needed. The trade-off is slightly higher dev effort to implement the light sensor logic, but it directly improves liveliness and clarity for users.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t user preference—it’s that auto-switching still assumes users *want* their interface to change without their say. A better alternative: ship a one-click toggle that remembers the user’s choice, with the system defaulting to dark but letting them override it permanently. Settle it by testing both options with five users—if more than half manually switch back within a day, the toggle wins.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a one-click dark/light toggle that remembers the user’s choice, defaulting to dark. This puts control in the user’s hands—no guessing about their preference, no friction in bright or dim rooms. The trade-off is slightly more UI clutter, but it avoids the bigger risk of annoying users by changing their interface without permission.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t clutter—it’s that a toggle still assumes users *will* engage with it. A better alternative: ship dark by default, but auto-switch only when the user *explicitly opts in* during onboarding. Settle it by testing both—if >70% of users keep the toggle untouched after a week, the auto-switch is dead weight.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default, a one-click toggle that remembers the user’s choice, and an optional onboarding prompt to auto-switch based on ambient light—only if users explicitly opt in.

Result: A dark-first interface with user-controlled flexibility, tested for preference retention. Owner: visualization-w1.
